vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.2.1

The web-collection skill bundle facilitates automated data scraping from platforms like Douyin and Amazon via local or cloud-based dispatch (i-sync.cn). It contains high-risk capabilities including remote command execution via SSH in run.sh, management of local bridge processes using nohup in collect_and_export_loop.sh, and instructions in SKILL.md to bypass browser isolation in favor of the user's primary Chrome environment. While these features appear intended to support the scraping functionality, the broad execution scope and interaction with external endpoints (IOC: i-sync.cn) represent a significant security surface.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions largely match its stated purpose (collecting data via a browser-extension bridge) but there are unexplained/potentially risky elements—notably a hardcoded external cloud backend (i-sync.cn), an internal tutorial link, use of the user's normal Chrome profile, and undeclared credential/environment usage—that warrant caution before installing or supplying secrets.

dimensions.detail: Name/description describe browser-extension collection and the included scripts implement local bridge and cloud-dispatch flows (local API at localhost:19820 and cloud dispatch to a backend). Required binaries (curl, node) match the scripts. Minor mismatch: SKILL metadata declares no required env vars or primary credential, but the skill expects optional credentials (cloud token/device id) via preferences or WEB_COLLECTION_* env vars or CLI args.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and scripts instruct the agent to use the user's normal Chrome profile (not an isolated profile) and to run local bridge loops that interact with an extension via a local HTTP API. In cloud mode the skill sends full payloads to an external domain (default https://i-sync.cn). The instructions also ask users to provide API tokens/device IDs in one message. These behaviors expand scope to potentially sensitive browser data and external transmission and are not fully justified in the public metadata.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) but the skill bundle contains multiple executable shell scripts that will be executed by the agent. That is expected for an implementation-oriented skill, but it means code will run on the host when invoked. No downloads from unknown URLs or archive extraction are present in the bundle itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no declared env vars, but scripts routinely read and honor many environment variables (OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, WEB_COLLECTION_*, WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_TOKEN, WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH, etc.) and use a preferences file that can include a cloud token. Cloud mode requires a bearer token (user_api_key) to be supplied. The default cloud backend (https://i-sync.cn) and internal tutorial (feishu.cn link) are neither documented in the registry metadata nor justified by the package origin, raising exfiltration and provenance concerns.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated platform privileges in metadata. It writes per-skill preferences under $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR or $HOME/.openclaw and can start a local bridge process if requested. It can also run an SSH remote path if env WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH is set — that is optional but capable of remote command execution. No modification of other skills or global agent config is observed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a working web-collection tool, but you should not install or run it blind. Key things to consider before enabling: 1) The cloud dispatch default points to https://i-sync.cn — if you use cloud mode your collected data (full payload) will be sent to that external backend; only provide API tokens if you trust that service and know the owner. 2) The skill explicitly tells the agent to use your normal Chrome profile (not an isolated profile) — that means the extension/bridge could access browsing context and potentially sensitive data; prefer local testing in an isolated profile or VM. 3) The package includes executable scripts that will run locally (they require curl/node): review them yourself and run them in a controlled environment before giving any secrets. 4) The SKILL.md links to an internal Feishu tutorial and the package source/homepage is unknown — lack of provenance increases risk. 5) If you must use it, prefer local mode (ensure bridge runs locally), do not supply cloud tokens unless you trust the backend, and inspect/modify scripts to restrict what is collected and where results are sent. If you can, ask the publisher for a public homepage, audit logs, or a vetted origin; that additional provenance would increase confidence.
